assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period compared: 1-31 October 2026 against 1-30 September 2026, since no period was specified in the question.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was about 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. Real events like sales and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period; it is not treated as a data error by itself.
Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 89.2%, order-level 91.6% and technical 92.9%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts for Harbor Bank debit cards only, not for the whole book.
The headline change of 0.41pp is statistically significant but small in practical terms.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 0.41pp from 89.6% (353,242 attempts) to 89.2% (430,580 attempts); the change is statistically significant (p = 5.18e-09) but not judged practically significant.
By payment method, the mix effect was -0.56pp and the like-for-like rate effect was +0.15pp, so mix shift more than explains the overall drop.
CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 7.2% of attempts while its success rate was 80.5% in September and 81.6% in October; it contributed -0.30pp of the -0.41pp change, mostly through mix (-0.36pp).
UPI share fell from 54.0% to 47.9%; UPI's own success rate was 92.8% and 93.1%.

The merchant group NovaMart grew from 6.1% to 18.8% of attempts, while its success rate went from 89.5% to 86.8%; it accounts for -0.50pp (123%) of the -0.41pp change. Merchant group is the top-ranked driver dimension.

Within payment methods, the largest genuine rate decline is Harbor Bank debit cards: 85.1% to 81.1% (down 4.01pp), contributing -0.17pp to the overall change. Meridian Bank debit (86.1% to 84.3%, -0.08pp) and Saffron Bank debit (86.5% to 85.0%, -0.05pp) also declined.

For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE failures rose from 0.50 to 6.09 per 100 attempts (74 to 1,091 failures), a rise of 5.59 per 100 attempts. Other failure codes were flat or lower, for example ACQ_TIMEOUT fell from 1.01 to 0.19 per 100 attempts.
Harbor Bank debit daily success rate shows a drop window from 21 Oct to 31 Oct (and a one-day drop on 17 Sep).
October success rate depends on the definition: attempt-level 89.2%, order-level 91.6%, technical 92.9%.

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 0.41pp, from 89.6% in September to 89.2% in October. The drop is statistically real but small; mix shift (growth of low-success EMI card payments) accounts for more than all of it, while like-for-like rates were roughly flat overall, with a genuine decline concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break CARD_EMI volume by merchant group and compare daily NovaMart share with the 18-31 Oct volume spike.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's share tripled, CARD_EMI's share more than doubled, and EMI has a structurally lower success rate (about 81%) than UPI (about 93%). The volume spike from 18 Oct onward is consistent with a sale.
hypotheses.text: A sale-driven surge from NovaMart pushed more EMI card volume, lowering the blended rate through mix rather than a worsening payment experience.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Confirm with Harbor Bank whether risk or fraud rules changed around 21 Oct and check whether declines concentrate on particular merchants or ticket sizes.
hypotheses.rationale: The decline is concentrated in one issuer and one payment method, and the failure-code shift is almost entirely risk declines, with the daily drop window starting 21 Oct.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules on debit cards around 21 Oct, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE and the genuine rate decline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare NovaMart's success rate within each payment method and issuer between the two periods.
hypotheses.rationale: The merchant-group view mixes rate and mix effects, and NovaMart's volume grew sharply in the same period.
hypotheses.text: NovaMart's own rate decline (89.5% to 86.8%) may partly reflect its higher EMI mix and the Harbor Bank issue rather than a NovaMart-specific problem.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules on debit cards around 21 Oct, causing the surge in ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE and the genuine rate decline.
recommendations.rationale: This is the largest like-for-like decline and the failure-code shift points to risk declines.
recommendations.text: Engage Harbor Bank on the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE increase on debit cards since about 21 Oct and ask whether rules changed or can be tuned.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A sale-driven surge from NovaMart pushed more EMI card volume, lowering the blended rate through mix rather than a worsening payment experience.
recommendations.rationale: Mix effect (-0.56pp) exceeded the total drop, driven by NovaMart and CARD_EMI growth.
recommendations.text: Report success rate by payment method and merchant group alongside the blended rate during sale periods, so mix-driven dips are not mistaken for performance problems.

Meridian Bank debit (86.1% to 84.3%, -0.08pp) and Saffron Bank debit (86.5% to 85.0%, -0.05pp) also declined.
recommendations.rationale: Both show statistically supported declines in debit card success rates, though smaller in size.
recommendations.text: Review the smaller declines at Meridian Bank and Saffron Bank debit cards to see whether they share the same cause as Harbor Bank.
